placementGuidelines: CAUTION - considered invasive in parts of Georgia and Florida, especially near coastal wetlands and marsh edges; not recommended for naturalized or habitat-restoration plantings under SERA's native-first approach. If grown, use physical edging barriers to control lateral spread, or contain in pots to prevent self-seeding/rhizome spread entirely, and deadhead before seed pods form. Adaptable to full sun-part shade; morning sun with afternoon shade protection often gives the most consistent bloom in intense summer heat. Drought-tolerant once established but responds well to consistent moisture; watch for root rot in heavy/poorly-drained soil - amend with coarse sand/perlite or grow in raised beds/containers. If leggy by midsummer, cut back hard to 6-8 inches; rebounds with a fresh bloom flush in 2-3 weeks.
